excerpt: Review the fees, authority, reporting, maintenance and exit clauses in a UAE property management agreement before appointing a landlord's manager.
introduction:
A property management agreement determines what the manager will do, how the landlord pays and who can make decisions about the home. A low advertised fee is only useful if the scope, other charges, reporting and authority limits are clear.

Review the contract for the exact property and intended rental strategy, and verify the manager's credentials with the responsible local authority.
takeaways: Define the services, fee basis and payment handling in writing.
Set repair approval limits, reporting, insurance and tenant communication responsibilities.
Check the duration, termination process and transfer of keys, deposits and records.

sections.heading: Define the manager's scope
sections.body:
List who markets the home, arranges viewings, screens tenants, prepares the lease, handles registration, collects rent and manages renewals. Specify whether inspections, move-in and move-out reports, rent collection and emergency attendance are included. A leasing-only service and ongoing management may have different scopes.

For Dubai, [DLD's licensed brokers service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/licensed-real-estate-brokers/?r=1) provides a way to check licensed brokers. Verify the manager’s company and authorisation for the relevant property management activity with the competent authority.

table.caption: Agreement checklist
rows: Percentage base, fixed charges, tax and third-party costs
Repair approval, emergencies and spending limits
Rent, tenant deposits, account and payout schedule
Notice, termination fees, records and keys

sections.heading: Compare the real cost of management
sections.body:
Ask whether the fee is based on rent due, rent collected or another amount, and whether VAT applies. Request separate charges for finding a tenant, renewal, advertising, inspection, call-outs and administration. Check whether contractor invoices include a management markup and who must approve it.

Imagine AED 80,000 collected rent and a sample 5% management fee based on that amount: AED 4,000 before any applicable tax or additional charges. At a sample 8%, the fee would be AED 6,400. These are arithmetic examples, not standard UAE fees or current quotations.

sections.heading: Control rent and deposits
sections.body:
Specify which account receives rent, when the manager transfers the landlord's share and how a statement reconciles income and deductions. Ask for invoices and receipts and establish who can authorise refunds. The agreement should explain how tenant deposits are held, documented and returned under the applicable rules.

Do not treat a refundable tenant deposit as rental income. Confirm what happens if rent is late or a payment fails, who communicates with the tenant and when the landlord must approve further action. Verify bank details independently and keep a record of each payment.

sections.heading: Set maintenance authority
sections.body:
Agree a spending limit for routine repairs and what constitutes an emergency. Specify how the manager contacts the owner, what happens if the owner cannot be reached and whether the limit applies per job or over a defined period. Request photographs, quotations, invoices and proof of completed work.

Ask how contractors are selected, whether the manager receives commissions and whether the owner can use a preferred contractor. Clarify responsibility for tenant-caused damage, warranty claims and common-area faults. An emergency provision should not become unlimited authority for unrelated improvements.

sections.heading: Review tenant and legal processes
sections.body:
Identify who prepares the lease, checks tenant documents, conducts inspections and registers or renews the tenancy where required. The [Dubai Land Department tenancy registration service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/register-renew-ejari-contract/) describes a Dubai process; check the current rules and authority in other emirates. The manager should not promise an outcome in a dispute.

If short stays are intended, verify the relevant local permit, building rules, guest handling, cleaning, platform fees and insurance before appointing an operator. A long-term management contract may not cover holiday-home activity.

sections.heading: Agree reporting and insurance
sections.body:
Set a reporting frequency and require a statement showing rent received, vacancy, deductions, maintenance, deposit movements and amounts paid to the owner. Agree how the owner can see supporting documents and how long records are retained. Ask how tenant and owner information will be protected and who may access it.

Confirm the building's policy and the owner's separate insurance needs. Check whether the manager holds any relevant cover and what it excludes. Insurance terms depend on the policy and do not automatically cover every loss or vacancy.

sections.heading: Read the exit provisions
sections.body:
Check the contract term, renewal, notice period, termination fee and circumstances in which either party may end it. Specify the handover of keys, tenant contacts, lease, deposits, maintenance history and outstanding rent. Ask how unpaid invoices or disputes will be reconciled.

If the property is sold, agree what happens to an existing tenant and the manager's authority. Ensure the owner can obtain records promptly and that no continuing marketing or payment authority survives beyond what was agreed. Seek legal advice if a clause is unclear.

sections.heading: Test the agreement against a real scenario
sections.body:
Ask the prospective manager to walk through a vacant month, an urgent repair and a tenant renewal. Request a sample statement and a written fee schedule. Compare several proposals on scope and controls, not only the percentage shown in an advertisement.

Ask who will communicate with the tenant outside normal office hours and whether the owner receives a copy of correspondence. Check the target response time, how missed payments are reported and whether legal proceedings require a separate appointment. These details make the difference between a service description and a workable arrangement. The agreement should reflect the property's actual use and the owner's availability.

sections.heading: Start with the property and its requirements
sections.body:
Use the [Ajman area guide](/journal/ajman-property-2026) and [RAK lifestyle guide](/journal/ras-al-khaimah-property-lifestyle) for local context. Browse [Aliyas UAE projects](/projects) and [contact Aliyas](/contact) for current property information. Verify the manager, local requirements and the agreement before signing.

For an existing lease, ask how the manager will obtain the contract, tenant deposit record, keys and maintenance history. Agree the opening balance and any work already authorised. Retain a copy of the signed agreement and check the first statement against the bank and the supporting invoices.
